mainTopic: Whether a בדיקה is needed before relations, and the ברייתא and ruling about a woman with no fixed וסת
overview: This amud first finishes a discussion about whether a husband must have his wife do a בדיקה before relations. רבא says that waking her to check would embarrass her. רב כהנא reports that the wives of great חכמים confirmed their husbands never required it. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא about a woman with no fixed וסת. רבי מאיר forbids her to her husband, takes away her כתובה and related rights, and requires a permanent divorce. רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס allows relations if she checks with two cloths, and אבא חנן says 'woe to her husband.' The גמרא explains each of רבי מאיר's rules, including why he may never remarry her: otherwise the גט could later be undone and her children become ממזרים. It gives two views of whom אבא חנן was answering. Then שמואל rules like רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, and the גמרא explains that this ruling is about a woman who handles טהרות. The פרק שמאי אומר then closes with הדרן.

steps.title: רבא rejects waking the wife to check
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב פפא that a sleeping wife should not be woken to do a בדיקה, because it would embarrass her in front of her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wise one, no! She would be embarrassed in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is pushing back on רב פפא's suggestion that the husband wake his wife so she can check herself before relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection is not about the strict law of purity. It is about human dignity: making her stop and think about her purity status in front of her husband is shameful for her. So we do not require it.

keyTerms.meaning: A nickname, 'wise one' or 'scholar', used when speaking to a colleague
She is shamed or made to look bad
In front of him (literally, 'before his face')

phrases.english: He said to him: Wise one, no!
phrases.notes: This is רבא answering רב פפא's idea from just before: that the husband should wake his wife so she can check.

phrases.english: For she would be demeaned before him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סוּדָנִי, לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב פפא's suggestion, which comes just before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that a sleeping wife must be woken to do a בדיקה before relations.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion ignores the embarrassment it would cause her.

steps.title: רב כהנא asks the Sages' wives
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports that he asked the wives of רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע whether their husbands required a בדיקה. They said no.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: I asked the wives of רב פפא and of רב הונא son of רב יהושע: when your husbands come home from the study hall, do they make you check first? They told me: No.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא brings real-life evidence: great חכמים did not require their wives to check before relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This supports the lenient view that no בדיקה is needed. The proof comes from what the חכמים actually did at home, not only from a ruling they said out loud.

keyTerms.meaning: Members of his household; here it means his wife
The study hall, the house of learning
They require
A self-check for blood

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
I asked the members of the household
phrases.notes: 'Members of the household' is a polite way of saying 'the wife.'

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב פָּפָּא וּדְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: of Rav Pappa and of Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua:
When the Sages come from the study hall,
do they require you to do an examination?
And they said to me: No.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: שְׁאֵלְתִּינְהוּ לְאִינָשֵׁי בֵּיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support from real practice to רבא's view that no בדיקה is required.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband does not need to have his wife do a בדיקה before relations.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The testimony of the wives of רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.

steps.title: Why not ask the Sages themselves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב כהנא asked the wives instead of asking the חכמים directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him ask them, the Sages themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by רב כהנא's method. It sets up the next step, which will explain why he asked the wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking the wives seems odd and indirect. The question pushes us to understand what kind of information רב כהנא was really looking for.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him ask them
Them themselves

phrases.english: But let him ask them themselves!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִישַׁיְּילִינְהוּ לְדִידְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how רב כהנא gathered his evidence.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's choice to ask the wives.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Asking the חכמים directly would seem to be the more natural and reliable way.

steps.title: They might be strict only on themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חכמים might be personally strict, so their wives were asked in order to learn what really happened at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps they are strict with themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the wives were asked: a חכם's personal habits might be stricter than the law he would rule for others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking the wives shows what the חכמים actually did. Since even in their own homes they did not require a בדיקה, this is a strong proof that it is truly not required.

keyTerms.meaning: They are strict
On themselves

steps.whatToRemember: No בדיקה is required before relations: waking her would embarrass her, and the wives of great חכמים confirmed it was never required.

phrases.english: Perhaps they are strict with themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא אִינְהוּ קָא מַחְמְירִי אַנַּפְשַׁיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the method: practice at home is better evidence than a ruling given out loud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Asking the חכמים directly would have been simpler.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wives show what was really done, and that is the clearest proof.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: a woman with no fixed cycle
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר: a woman with no fixed וסת is forbidden to her husband, loses her כתובה and related rights, and must be divorced permanently.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: a woman who has no fixed cycle is forbidden to have relations. She has no כתובה, no payment for produce, no support, and no worn clothes. He must divorce her and may never take her back. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by bringing a ברייתא. It begins with רבי מאיר's very strict opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a fixed וסת, she can never know when bleeding may come, so רבי מאיר forbids relations entirely. Because of that, she also loses the money rights that come with marriage, and the marriage must end.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed, predictable menstrual cycle
To have marital relations
The marriage contract payment given to her if divorced or widowed
Payment for the produce of her property that the husband used
Food and support
Her worn items from the dowry, returned to her

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume this is the final הלכה. It is only רבי מאיר's view, and the next step brings a lenient opinion.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A woman who does not have a fixed cycle
is forbidden to have relations,
and she has no marriage contract payment,
nor produce, nor support,
nor worn clothes,
and he must divorce her and never take her back,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אִשָּׁה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ וֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a woman with no וסת is forbidden to her husband, loses her financial rights, and must be divorced permanently.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: she may, with two cloths
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס rules that she may have relations if she checks with two cloths, and the result decides her status.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: she has relations using two examination cloths. They can hurt her, and they can help her.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא disagrees with רבי מאיר and allows relations with careful checking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of forbidding her completely, she checks before and after relations. If blood is found, that is bad for her; if the cloths are clean, she stays permitted to her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: Examination cloths (literally 'witnesses'), used to check for blood
They harmed her (if blood is found)
They helped her (if clean)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:
She has relations with two examination cloths,
phrases.notes: One cloth before relations and one after.

phrases.english: they may harm her, they may help her.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר: מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת בִּשְׁנֵי עִדִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר's ban on relations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She may have relations if she checks with two cloths; the cloths decide her status.

steps.title: אבא חנן: woe to her husband
steps.stepSummary: In the name of אבא חנן they said: 'Woe to her husband.'
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of אבא חנן they said: Woe to her husband!
steps.whatsHappening: A third voice in the ברייתא adds a short, sharp remark about the husband's hard situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The remark shows concern for the husband married to a woman with no fixed וסת. The ברייתא does not explain it, but the גמרא does later, in steps 14-15.

keyTerms.meaning: Woe to him
Her husband

phrases.english: In the name of Abba Chanan they said:
Woe to her husband!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא חָנָן אָמְרוּ: אוֹי לוֹ לְבַעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further comment to the ברייתא's debate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא חנן expresses distress for the husband of such a woman.

steps.title: Why she is forbidden to have relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining רבי מאיר's rulings: she is forbidden because she might bleed during relations and cause her husband to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'She is forbidden to have relations': perhaps she will ruin him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is now going through רבי מאיר's ruling clause by clause, starting with the ban on relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she has no predictable cycle, bleeding could start during relations. That would cause her husband to transgress, so רבי מאיר forbids relations entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: She ruins or causes him to stumble into sin

phrases.english: 'She is forbidden to have relations':
perhaps she will ruin him.
phrases.notes: Meaning she might begin bleeding during relations, which would make her husband sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲסוּרָה לְשַׁמֵּשׁ — דִּילְמָא מְקַלְקְלָה לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to explain the first clause of רבי מאיר's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban exists because she might bleed during relations.

steps.title: Why she has no כתובה
steps.stepSummary: She has no כתובה because she is not fit for relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she has no כתובה': since she is not fit for relations, she has no כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next clause of רבי מאיר's ruling: why she loses her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובה is tied to a marriage that includes marital relations. Since she cannot have relations, she does not receive a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit or suitable
Marital relations

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, the loss of her money rights flows from the ban on relations: no relations means no כתובה.

phrases.english: 'And she has no marriage contract payment':
since she is not fit for relations,
she has no marriage contract payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לָהּ כְּתוּבָּה — כֵּיוָן דְּלָא חַזְיָא לְבִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the clause-by-clause explanation of רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She loses her כתובה because she is unfit for relations.

steps.title: She also loses the extra rights written in the marriage contract
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that she loses פירות, מזונות and בלאות because the conditions of a כתובה are treated like the כתובה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: She also gets no payment for produce, no food support, and no worn clothing back, because the conditions of the marriage contract are treated just like the marriage contract.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues explaining רבי מאיר's ruling. It gives the reason she also loses the other money rights listed in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said she loses her כתובה because she is not fit for relations. Here the גמרא adds that the other rights are only תנאי כתובה, conditions attached to the כתובה. So if the כתובה goes, they go with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Conditions of the marriage contract, the rights that come along with the כתובה
Are like, are treated the same as

phrases.english: And not produce, and not sustenance,
and not worn clothes:
the conditions of a marriage contract are like the marriage contract itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָאֵי כְּתוּבָּה כִּכְתוּבָּה דָּמוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 9's reason for losing the כתובה to the related rights listed in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Conditions of the כתובה share the status of the כתובה, so she loses them all.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא need to say he can never remarry her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'he must divorce her and never take her back' and asks: isn't that obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He must divorce her and never remarry her.' Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא and challenges it. If she is forbidden to him, why would anyone think he could take her back?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem behind the divorce, no fixed וסת, has not gone away. So it seems obvious that he cannot remarry her, and the ברייתא should not need to say it. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! A challenge that a statement seems unnecessary
He must send her out, meaning divorce her
He may never take her back

phrases.english: And he must divorce her, and never take her back.
That is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the money clauses to the divorce clause of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's words 'and never take her back'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the reason she is forbidden is still there, saying he cannot remarry her seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Even if her cycle later becomes regular, he may not remarry her
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed for a case where she later got a fixed וסת. He still may not remarry her, because sometimes such a woman marries someone else and then becomes regular.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where she later became fixed. You might have said he may take her back. So it teaches us that he may not, because sometimes she goes and marries someone else and then becomes fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule is not obvious. It applies even after she gets a regular cycle, when we might have thought he could take her back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new case is that the problem has been fixed. The הוה אמינא was that since the reason is gone, he may remarry her. The ברייתא says no, because of what might happen when she marries someone else and then becomes fixed. The next step explains the danger.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for, used to show the special case where a rule is not obvious
You might have said, introducing the mistaken first thought
It teaches us, introducing the real point
She was fixed, meaning she got a regular cycle

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the danger is about remarrying this woman while she is still not fixed. The case is that she already became fixed, and he still may not take her back.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where she later became fixed.
You might have said he may take her back.
So it teaches us that he may not,
because sometimes she goes and marries someone else, and then becomes fixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא דַּהֲדַרָה וְאִתַּקַּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא by limiting the rule to a case where it is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (לא צריכא): the rule applies even after she becomes fixed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once she has a fixed וסת, the reason for the divorce is gone, so he may remarry her.
steps.terutzMaskana: He may never remarry her, even after she becomes fixed, because of what could happen if she marries another man and then becomes fixed.

steps.title: The danger: he could claim the divorce was a mistake
steps.stepSummary: If she becomes fixed while married to someone else, the first husband might say he never would have divorced her, making the גט void and her children ממזרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he might say: 'Had I known it would turn out like this, even if you gave me a hundred מנה, I would not have divorced her!' Then the גט turns out to be void, and her children are ממזרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by explaining what could go wrong. This is why the divorce must be final from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband could later say he divorced her only because of a problem that went away, the גט might be treated as given by mistake. Then she was never really divorced, and children from her second husband would be ממזרים. Telling him at the start that he can never take her back means he divorces her knowing it is final.

keyTerms.meaning: A hundred מנה, a huge sum of money
A void bill of divorce
Children from a forbidden union, here from a married woman with another man

steps.whatToRemember: He may never remarry her, even after she becomes fixed. This keeps the divorce final, so he cannot later say it was a mistake and make her later children ממזרים.

phrases.english: And he might say: 'If I had known it would turn out like this,'

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הֱיִיתֶם נוֹתְנִין לִי מֵאָה מָנֶה —
phrases.english: even if you had given me a hundred מנה,
phrases.notes: A מנה is a hundred דינרים, so this means a very large amount of money.

phrases.english: I would not have divorced her!'
And the bill of divorce turns out to be void, and her children are ממזרים.
phrases.notes: He means her children from the second husband, since she would still count as married to the first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילּוּ הָיִיתִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁכָּךְ הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes step 12's answer by spelling out the danger.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reason behind the case limitation
steps.terutzMaskana: Making the divorce final prevents a later claim of a mistaken divorce, which could make the גט void and the children ממזרים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how חז"ל protect a גט from being undone by a husband's later regret.

steps.title: First view: אבא חנן was speaking against רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes אבא חנן's 'Woe to her husband' and gives the first view: he said it to רבי מאיר, because he holds the husband must pay her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of אבא חנן they said: 'Woe to her husband!' Some say he said this to רבי מאיר, because he holds the husband has to pay her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last line of the ברייתא from step 7 and asks whom אבא חנן was answering. The first view says he was arguing with רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said she loses her כתובה (step 9). By this view, אבא חנן disagrees: the husband must still pay. So 'woe to her husband' means the poor husband loses his wife and must pay the כתובה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: To pay her the כתובה money

phrases.english: In the name of אבא חנן they said:
'Woe to her husband!'

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר אֲמַר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Some say he said this to רבי מאיר,
because he has to pay her her marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר אֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the divorce clause to the last clause of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By this view, אבא חנן disagrees with רבי מאיר and holds the husband must pay the כתובה.

steps.title: Second view: אבא חנן was speaking against רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס
steps.stepSummary: Others say אבא חנן said it to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, because she might ruin the husband by causing him to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he said it to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, because she will ruin him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second view about whom אבא חנן was answering. Here he was arguing with the lenient view that allows relations with checking cloths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס allowed relations if she checks with two cloths (step 6). By this view, אבא חנן says that is too risky. She may see blood during relations and 'ruin' him by causing him to sin, so 'woe to her husband' if he relies on the checks.

keyTerms.meaning: She ruins him, meaning she causes him to sin

steps.whatToRemember: Two views on אבא חנן: either he argues with רבי מאיר about money (the husband must pay the כתובה), or he argues with רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס about the איסור (relations are too risky).

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס קָאָמַר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: And some say he was saying it to רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס,
because she will ruin him.
phrases.notes: Ruin him means she might see blood during relations and cause him to sin, the same worry as in step 8.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס קָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second way to understand whom אבא חנן was answering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By this view, אבא חנן disagrees with רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס and forbids relations, because she may cause her husband to sin.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.
steps.whatsHappening: After the two versions of whom אבא חנן was arguing with, the גמרא brings a ruling: שמואל holds like רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס allows a woman without a fixed וסת to stay married and rely on checking herself, instead of having to be divorced. שמואל rules that way. This ruling sets up the question in the next steps: what case is שמואל talking about?

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical ruling follows this opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line about a woman without a fixed וסת: she does not have to be divorced.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says:
The halakha follows Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus.
phrases.notes: He's the one from step 6 who lets her have relations if she checks with two cloths.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the ברייתא's dispute between רבי מאיר (step 5) and רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס (step 6).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס about a woman without a fixed וסת.

steps.title: If the ruling is about טהרות, שמואל already said it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case שמואל means. If it is a woman who handles טהרות, he already said that on another occasion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about what case did he say this? If it is about a woman who handles pure items, didn't שמואל already say this one time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a two-sided challenge. Here is the first side: if the ruling is about a woman who handles טהרות, it is a repeat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל already has a known ruling that a woman without a וסת must check herself, and that ruling was explained as being about a woman who handles טהרות. So reading this new ruling the same way makes it unnecessary. The second side of the challenge comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And about what case?
A woman who handles ritually pure foods or items
One time, meaning he already said it before

phrases.english: And regarding what case?
If it is about a woman engaged in handling pure items,
didn't Shmuel already say it one time!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמַאי? אִי בַּעֲסוּקָה בִּטְהָרוֹת, הָא אַמְרַהּ שְׁמוּאֵל חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what case the ruling in step 16 covers.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling like רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ruling is about a woman who handles טהרות, it repeats something שמואל already said.

steps.title: If it is not about טהרות, שמואל needs no checking for the husband
steps.stepSummary: If the ruling is about a woman who does not handle טהרות, שמואל holds that checking just for the husband is not needed. The proof is his statement that was explained as being about טהרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is about a woman who does not handle pure items, didn't he say that anything only for her husband does not need checking? For רבי זירא said in the name of רבי אבא בר ירמיה in the name of שמואל: 'A woman without a fixed cycle may not have relations until she checks,' and we explained this as being about a woman who handles pure items.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second side of the challenge. Reading the ruling as being about a woman who does not handle טהרות clashes with שמואל's own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's statement 'אסורה לשמש עד שתבדוק' was explained as being only about a woman who handles טהרות. That shows two things. First, he already ruled on the טהרות case, which is the repeat from step 17. Second, for a woman who checks only for her husband, no בדיקה is needed. So both readings of the new ruling run into trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: We established it as referring to a certain case
Does not require

phrases.english: And if it is about a woman not engaged in handling pure items,
didn't he say: anything that is only for her husband
does not require an examination,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר יִרְמְיָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbi Abba bar Yirmeya said that Shmuel said:
"A woman who does not have a fixed cycle
is forbidden to have relations until she examines herself,"
and we explained it as being about a woman engaged in handling pure items!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ עֲסוּקָה בִּטְהָרוֹת, הָא אָמַר כֹּל לְבַעְלַהּ לָא בָּעֲיָא בְּדִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided challenge that began in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading שמואל's ruling as being about a woman who does not handle טהרות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל holds that no בדיקה is needed just for the husband, so a ruling requiring checks for that woman would contradict him.

steps.title: Different students passed down different rulings from שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The person who teaches one statement in שמואל's name does not teach the other, so neither one is a repeat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches this statement does not teach that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first side of the challenge. The two rulings came to us through different students, so it is no problem that they seem to say the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling really is about a woman who handles טהרות. רב יהודה passed it down as 'הלכה כרבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס,' and the other version came through רבי אבא בר ירמיה, quoted by רבי זירא, as 'אסורה לשמש עד שתבדוק.' Each line reported שמואל's view once, so there is no repetition.

keyTerms.term: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי הָא לָא מַתְנֵי הָא
keyTerms.meaning: Whoever teaches this does not teach that: two versions passed down by different people

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the two rulings disagree. It means one ruling from שמואל reached us in two forms through two different people.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's ruling like רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס is about a woman who handles טהרות. The two reports of his view come from different students, so neither one is a repeat.

phrases.english: The one who teaches this statement
does not teach that one.
phrases.notes: So the ruling is about טהרות after all, and the 'he already said it' problem goes away.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי הָא לָא מַתְנֵי הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 17-18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements were assumed to come through the same line of tradition from שמואל, so one would be an unneeded repeat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ruling was reported by a different student, so the ruling can be about טהרות without any repetition.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק שמאי אומר
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the first פרק of מסכת נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, שמאי אומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the first פרק, שמאי אומר, with the traditional farewell line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן at the end of a פרק expresses the learner's wish and commitment to come back and learn it again. It is not part of the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, said at the end of a פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, Shammai Omer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ שַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of the first פרק of נדה, שמאי אומר.
